findings.quote: but rather to devote all their effort to discovering and recording what was truly said
findings.problem: Greek: τὰ κατ᾽ ἀλήθειαν ῥηθέντα καθ᾽ ὅσον οἷόν τε πολυπραγμονήσαντας διασαφεῖν — 'as far as possible, having investigated, to make clear what was truly said'. The qualifier καθ᾽ ὅσον οἷόν τε is dropped and replaced by an absolute 'all their effort'.
findings.proposed_fix: but rather, as far as possible, to investigate and set out clearly what was truly said

findings.quote: This principle having long since been firmly fixed in everyone’s mind
findings.problem: Greek: πάλαι δὲ τούτου κεκυρωμένου βεβαίως ἐν ταῖς ἑκάστων γνώμαις — the thing long since confirmed in each man's judgment is the (lost-context) matter, i.e. the decision for war; nothing in the Greek says 'principle'. Referent of τούτου is not in the extant text, so 'principle' is invented.
findings.proposed_fix: This (decision) having long since been firmly confirmed in the judgment of each

units.note: Antecedent of τούτου lost with the preceding text; the English should not supply 'principle'.

findings.quote: appointed two envoys with full powers
findings.problem: Greek: κατέστησαν πρεσβευτὰς αὐτοκράτορας, followed by five names: Γίσκων Στρυτάνος, Ἀμίλκας, Μίσδης, Γιλλίμας, Μάγων. The number is five, not two.
findings.proposed_fix: appointed five envoys with full powers

findings.quote: If that was not the course they chose, then they must consider once more
findings.problem: Greek: εἰ δὲ μή, τότε πάλιν βουλεύεσθαι — 'otherwise (i.e. if the order is utterly overbearing and unexpected), then deliberate again'. The English makes the condition refer to a course of action they might not choose, misreading εἰ δὲ μή.
findings.proposed_fix: Otherwise, they must then consider once more

findings.quote: in the dockyard of the six-banked ships.
findings.problem: Greek: εἰς τὸ τῆς ἑκκαιδεκήρους νεώριον *** — 'sixteen-banked' (ἑκκαιδεκήρης), singular ship, not six; and the Greek breaks off with a lacuna (***) after νεώριον, which the English reads as a complete sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: in the dockyard of the sixteen-banked ship [...]

units.note: The envoys' clause ἐὰν αὐτοὶ μὲν παραχωρήσωσι τῶν ὅπλων, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ λαβόντες ἀποπλεύσωσιν is awkward and its subject is not certain; current English is an acceptable reading, left alone. Numbers (more than 200,000 arms, 2,000 catapults) correct.

findings.quote: All the senators, crying out in horror, were left as though paralyzed by the shock.
findings.problem: Greek: οἱ δὲ πάντες ἅμ᾽ ἀνακεκραγότες ἐξ αὐτῆς οἱονεὶ παρελύθησαν — 'all of them, crying out together, were at once as if paralysed'. 'Senators' is not in the Greek (the group is unspecified in the extant text).
findings.proposed_fix: All of them cried out together and were at once as though paralyzed.

findings.problem: Greek: οὐκέτι συνέβαινε γίνεσθαι τὴν ἀλογίαν — ἀλογία here most likely 'speechless stupor' (contrast with the preceding παρελύθησαν and the action that follows), i.e. the stupor no longer continued; 'no more restraint' reverses the sense. Meaning of ἀλογία is somewhat uncertain.

findings.quote: and still others hurried toward the gates of the city
findings.problem: Greek: οἱ δὲ πρὸς τὰς πύλας τῆς πόλεως *** — the sentence breaks off in a lacuna with no verb; the English supplies 'hurried' and reads as complete.
findings.proposed_fix: and others [... text lost ...] to the gates of the city

findings.quote: When men are deliberating from scratch, they should take even greater care to avoid suffering harm than to do harm to their enemies.
findings.problem: Greek: ὁ Σκιπίων ἔφη, * ** ὅταν ἐξ ἀκεραίου βουλεύωνται, καὶ πλείω ποιεῖσθαι πρόνοιαν... — a lacuna (* **) follows ἔφη, and the speech begins mid-sentence at ὅταν; the English presents a smooth, complete quotation, inventing the main clause ('they should').
findings.proposed_fix: [...] when they are deliberating with the matter still open, and to take more forethought not to suffer any harm than to do harm to the enemy.

findings.quote: Scipio’s statement and his handling of the situation
findings.problem: Greek: τῇ τοῦ Σκιπίωνος ὁμολογίᾳ καὶ τῷ χειρισμῷ τῶν πραγμάτων — ὁμολογία is 'agreement/compact' (here Scipio's arrangement, probably with Phameas), not 'statement'.
findings.proposed_fix: Scipio’s agreement and his handling of affairs

units.note: The bracketed Greek [πάλιν ἄλλον πρὸς ἐκεῖνον: τί ἀκήκοας] indicates that 'What have you heard?' is put by another speaker to Porcius, whereas the English gives it to Porcius himself; the bracket is an editorial/corrupt insertion, so no fix is proposed. Cato identification (Marcus Porcius) and the Homeric tag (Il. 10 / Od. 10.495 'he alone has wits, the rest flit as shadows') are right.
